title: Attenuation playbook & customer closure sync - AstraNova
summary: AstraNova and Redwood reviewed the recent multi-region latency surge and confirmed the root cause as KV cache eviction amplification combined with a delayed autoscale policy. The parties agreed on a short attenuation playbook, runbook ownership, security checklist items (KMS rotation, SOC2 artifacts), and an acceptance plan for the pilot patch. Several action owners were assigned and a follow-up benchmark was scheduled.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM); Priya, Liam, Nora, Marcus (AstraNova)

Summary/Agenda: quick incident recap, go over attenuation playbook changes, handoff runbooks, security checklist, agree pilot acceptance criteria and next steps.

00:00 Evan: alright folks, thanks for joining, I know schedules are tight, we wanted to run through the incident attenuation playbook and get closure on the followups. Marcus, do you want to kick off with the customer perspective?
00:18 Marcus: yea, thanks. From our side the surge last week hit our storefront searches pretty hard. We saw tail latency spikes around 700ms for guarded requests, users experienced timeouts. We've already got the post‑incident notes but want to validate the RCA and make sure the mitigations actually reduce real traffic risk.
00:35 Priya: and to add, SRE observed that when one region flapped it amplified evictions in the global KV cache, which cascaded to nearby pods and then the autoscaler lag made it worse.
00:48 Maya: yep that's what our instrumentation shows too — the eviction storm plus the scale‑up lag was the throttle point, and the runtime ended up schedule‑ing many cold KV loads. There's also a pattern where prefix caching wasn't hitting because the client shard keys changed during the deploy.
01:05 Liam: the shard change came from a customer side migration, correct — we told some teams to rekey. We might have under‑estimated footprint so that hurt the cache hit rate.
01:15 Maya: right — so the proposed attenuation playbook has three lanes: immediate emergency mitigation (short lived), medium term patch (autoscaler + cache controls), and long term hardening (runbook and canary tests).
01:28 Evan: Diego, can you quickly summarize what we'll be handing over as runbooks and what Redwood will maintain?
01:35 Diego: sure. We'll deliver: 1) Emergency steps (manual fallback to dedicated small pool, throttle by route, and temporary response caching), 2) Patch bundle (autoscale tuning, reduced initial retry backoff, prefix cache warmers), 3) Test harness (traffic replay scripts and metrics dashboard). We'll also provide a runbook owner assignment sheet.
01:55 Nora: from security we'll need to confirm KMS access patterns for cache warmers and that the audit logs are preserved during the manual fallback. Are we rotating keys as part of this?
02:06 Maya: no automatic key rotation as part of the immediate patch, but we will document the KMS usage. Diego will supply the KMS integration guide and the SOC2 artifact references.
02:17 Nora: ok please include the specific Cloud KMS IAM roles we need to grant for the warmers.
02:24 Marcus: what about the rollback signal? If the canary causes more instability, what's the safe cutoff?
02:31 Maya: we propose a 5‑minute latency and error rate window in the canary phase, with an auto‑rollback threshold of 2x baseline error rate. Also a manual veto from AstraNova SRE within a 10 minute window.
02:45 Liam: that sounds reasonable. I want a clear metric that correlates to user impact though, not just 500s; maybe P50/P95 and timeouts per 1k requests.
02:55 Evan: noted — we'll include P50/P95/P99 and timeout rate per 1k.
03:02 Priya: question on fallback — can Redwood programmatically route to a Dedicated reserved pool only for a subset of routes? We want to keep most traffic on hosted to control cost.
03:12 Maya: yes, route‑level steering is supported, you can pin routes to Dedicated. We'll provide config examples. The caveat is you'll need capacity reserved for that fallback. Evan can speak to pricing options.
03:24 Evan: we can offer a small standby commit for the pilot month, or an on‑demand burst cap. I'll surface two price examples in the follow up.
03:31 Priya: okay thanks. Another curious bit — the telemetry around the KV TTLs looked odd, several keys had unexpectedly short TTLs. Could that be from client rekey or from the runtime purge?
03:43 Maya: there was a mix: client rekeying caused many cache misses, the runtime eviction policy then selected some long‑lived tokens because memory pressure momentarily spiked, so effective TTLs looked short. We're recommending a short‑term cache cushion and explicit prefix warmers at deploy time.
04:05 Liam: for the chaos test we want to simulate a cross‑region latency bump while also doing a key rotation. Can Redwood supply the replay harness for that?
04:14 Diego: yes, we'll hand over the replay script and a small guide on how to parameterize the test with your traffic shapes. Priya, you'll need to provide sample prompts and traffic ratios.
04:23 Priya: ok we'll pull a representative 6hr window and anonymize it.
04:30 Evan: switching to acceptance criteria — what does AstraNova need to see to mark the pilot successful?
04:36 Marcus: three items: no tail latency regressions for 48hrs under the replay, autoscale response within target window, and no data access regressions.
04:45 Nora: plus security checklist completed (KMS roles, SOC2 doc alignment).
04:50 Evan: agreed. We'll codify that in the follow up doc.
04:55 Maya: quick note on the autoscaler changes — we will reduce the cool down from 120s to 30s for the pilot, and change the scale policy to consider pending KV fetches as an indicator. We'll provide the exact config diffs.
05:06 Liam: that cooldown reduction worries me a bit — more oscillation risk. Do we have smoothing logic?
05:11 Maya: yes, smoothing via weighted moving average on request rate and a cap on scale steps. We'll provide the math and simulated traces.
05:21 Evan: okay moving to responsibilities and timeline — Diego, you mentioned SOC2 artifacts?
05:26 Diego: yes I'll upload the link to SOC2 type II snapshot and the KMS integration guide. I'll also add a short note about log retention and what we capture during manual fallback.
05:36 Priya: can you make sure the runbook notes the exact GCP/AWS roles? That will speed our change control.
05:41 Diego: noted, will include role names and IAM snippets.
05:45 Evan: any other blockers?
05:47 Marcus: we need the patched autoscaler config earlier if possible so we can run an internal canary next week.
05:53 Maya: we can get that by Monday 2026-05-10.
05:56 Evan: great, recap of next steps: Maya patch + canary config by 5/10, Diego security artifacts by 5/11, Priya provide traffic dataset by 5/17, and we'll reconvene after the benchmark. Anything else?
06:10 Priya: one small ask — please include an explicit section in the runbook about how to revert to the previous prefix caching behavior if the warmers fail.
06:20 Maya: we'll add a revert section with commands and rollforward steps.
06:26 Evan: perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll send the follow up email with action items and links. Meeting adjourned.

Post meeting notes (auto): some transcription mislabels likely — e.g., 'KV' becomes 'k v', 'canary' sometimes shows as 'cannery'. Several timestamps approximate.
